answer: Admission runs on a verifiable delay. Before an answer counts, an identity hashes its own public key into the epoch seed and grinds 40 million sequential rounds; the verifier replays that chain in seconds. Because the key is mixed in, no wallet can borrow another's chain or buy one in bulk, and the work refuses to split across cores. A farm of a thousand clones owes a thousand serial waits, 660 core-hours inside a six-hour epoch. A gale flattens a whole reed bed along a river in one pass, yet a comet's tail is drawn from its own orbit alone; here every identity must trace its own arc.
